clue.text: Lord Frederick maybe thrives without work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the reworked letters sit around the piece for work
maybe says the letters of thrives are only one possible arrangement, so rework them

parts.note: op is the standard short form of opus, a work

explanation.surface: A nobleman called Frederick apparently prospers without having to labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal and 'without' means outside, its old sense. Lord Frederick Verisopht is the foolish young aristocrat in Dickens's novel Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gave this surname to the dim-witted young lord in Nicholas Nickleby, whose first name is Frederick.

clue.text: Change of air, perhaps ?.

parts.note: read not as a trip for one's health but as a reworking of a tune, an air

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a change of scene for health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of air' suggests a holiday for the health; 'air' is a melody, and a reworked melody is a musical form.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a reworked version of a theme is a variation, and any alteration is also a variation.

clue.text: Entangle a composer

explanation.surface: A command to tangle up a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle threads into a knot is to ravel them, and Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero.

clue.text: Fiddling a bit over gin distribution

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece stands above the second

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece, a bit

indicators.note: distribution means the letters of gin are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Playing the violin a little, while gin is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges GIN as ING, and 'over' puts SCRAP above it. 'Fiddling' suggests cheating, but it is playing a violin, scraping the bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraping is a mocking word for poor violin playing, sawing at the strings.

clue.text: French statesman has river in mind

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'

explanation.surface: A French politician has a waterway on his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word, and the pieces simply sit side by side. Raymond Poincaré was French president during the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Poincaré was French prime minister and president in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Special antitude for money-making

parts.note: a gift or flair (antitude is the page's misprint for aptitude), and also an ancient weight of silver, the coin the servants traded with in the parable to make money

explanation.surface: A real gift for earning a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The page misprints 'aptitude' as 'antitude'. In the Gospel parable of the talents, servants are entrusted with sums of money and judged on what they made of them; that parable gave the word its sense of natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift is a talent, and a talent was also a large unit of silver money in the ancient world.

clue.text: She makes the most of our conquest

indicators.note: most of means one letter, the last, is dropped from the word supplied

parts.note: to a British reader the Norman Conquest of 1066 is the conquest of the nation

explanation.surface: A woman gets the greatest advantage from something the speaker has won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes the' is link material; 'most of' cuts the final N from NORMAN. The Norman Conquest of England in 1066 is the event a British setter calls 'our conquest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name, and the title heroine of Bellini's opera, so a female figure answers to 'She'.

clue.text: Animal ruins first-class turn

indicators.note: ruins says the pieces are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: A1 means first-class, and the digit 1 reads as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature wrecks a top-quality performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 written as AI, plus TURN, gives AITURN, which 'ruins' rearranges. 'ruins' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutria, or coypu, is a large South American rodent farmed for its fur.

clue.text: Rustic transporter returned to make hay, but withdrew

indicators.note: returned means the word for the carrier is read back to front

parts.note: a carter drives a cart on the farm, carrying goods
to ted is to spread out mown grass to dry into hay

explanation.surface: A country driver came back to bring in the harvest but backed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives RETRAC, and 'but' is a link word. Ted is a farming verb for turning mown grass so it dries into hay.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something back, a remark or a claw, is to retract it; the past tense means withdrew.

clue.text: A feature in the main part of the church

parts.note: the main is the open sea, and an isle is something that stands out in it

explanation.surface: A notable feature in the central section of a church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, an old poetic sense, not 'main part'. A plus ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage or side division of a church, alongside the nave.

clue.text: Is always without right back in game

indicators.note: back says the whole string built from these pieces is read in the opposite direction
without in its old sense of outside: the letter for right stands at the edge of the word for always

parts.note: taken as written
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: Something exists forever without being correct again during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: IS, then R outside EVER, gives ISREVER; 'back' turns the lot to read REVERSI. Reversi is the board game of flipping black-and-white counters, sold as Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversi is a two-player board game of capturing and turning over discs.

clue.text: Is prone to swallow a dram? An understatement!

indicators.note: to swallow means the first word takes the second inside it, as a mouth does

parts.note: someone prone, lying flat, lies
a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram

explanation.surface: Someone sprawled flat is ready to knock back a whisky, and that is putting it mildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' signals the container. 'Is prone' looks like 'is inclined', but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that asserts by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad', a form of deliberate understatement.

clue.text: As it was with a grey mare with this

definitions.text: As it was with a grey mare with this

parts.words: As it was with a grey mare with this
parts.note: the old grey mare of the folk song Widdecombe Fair fell sick and died; a phrase meaning finished for someone completes 'it was ... with' the mare

explanation.surface: A hint at the fate of a tired old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'it's all up with him' means he is finished. In the Devon folk song Widdecombe Fair, Tom Pearce's old grey mare dies after carrying seven riders to the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'it is all up with someone' means they are done for, as the mare in the song was.

clue.text: The post man?

parts.note: read not as a letter carrier but as a man seeking a post, a job or an office

explanation.surface: Someone who delivers the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the postman; the question mark invites the other reading, the man after a post or position.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing for an appointment or election is an applicant for a post.

clue.text: Soldiers in arms ?

parts.note: the foot soldiers of an army, with a pun on babies, 'infants in arms', still carried

explanation.surface: Fighting men in the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers in arms' sounds like comrades-in-arms; the question mark points to babes in arms, the tiny 'infants' inside the word for foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantry are soldiers who fight on foot, and the word holds 'infant', a baby carried in arms.

clue.text: Eccentric misfit she shows belief in charms

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An odd outsider of a woman is revealed as superstitious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges MISFIT and SHE; 'shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetishism is the worship of objects thought to have magical power, such as amulets or talismans.

clue.text: Half the letters matter?

definitions.meaning: the first half of the alphabet runs from A to M, thirteen of the twenty-six letters
the smallest particle of matter that keeps an element's identity

explanation.surface: Does half of the alphabet really count for anything?
explanation.definitionFit: The run from A to M covers half the alphabet, and that phrase spoken is the tiny particle that ordinary matter is built from.

clue.text: Scoundrel intended to see about one's credit reduction

indicators.note: about means the word for intended goes round the other pieces

parts.note: meant means intended, as in 'meant well'
one is I, so one's is I'S
CR, the reduced or shortened form of credit

explanation.surface: A rogue planned to look into lowering a person's credit limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is link material; 'about' puts IS and CR inside MEANT. 'reduction' means the abbreviation CR, not a cut in credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, a villain or rogue.

clue.text: Doctor's prescription for renewed strain ?

parts.note: fresh means renewed, as in a fresh start
a strain is a tune, an air

explanation.surface: What a doctor orders for nervous tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' suggests stress, but here it is a melody. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors traditionally advise patients to get out into the open, breathing clean outdoor atmosphere.

clue.text: Bad fit in light sole, perhaps

indicators.note: in means the reworked letters sit inside the word for light

parts.note: a flash is a burst of light

indicators.note: bad says the letters of fit are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: A poorly fitting shoe sole that weighs little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' gives TFI and 'in' signals the container. 'sole' looks like a shoe part, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sole is a fish that lies flat on the seabed, with both eyes on one side.

clue.text: Any key except one

parts.note: a musical pitch named by a letter, read as '...', a description that fits every key but the one called E

explanation.surface: Every key on the ring but a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the answer reads NOT E: any musical key except one, the key of E. A key on a keyboard also sounds a single musical tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical tone such as C or G names a key, and every such pitch but E is literally 'not E'.

clue.text: Wordsworth's work's set to music

definitions.meaning: The Prelude is Wordsworth's long autobiographical poem; the 's means 'the Prelude is'
introductory pieces of music, often for piano, as by Chopin

explanation.surface: A poet's writing has been given a musical setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's great poem is The Prelude, and short opening or stand-alone pieces of music bear the same name in the plural.

clue.text: Passages for everyone? Yes, possibly

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of yes may be put in another order

explanation.surface: Are corridors open to all? Perhaps they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' gives EYS, and 'for' is a link word. 'Passages' suggests extracts from a book; here they are narrow lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleys are narrow lanes or passageways between buildings.

clue.text: Like 13 on foot ?

parts.note: soldiers on the march keep time together, and the same words name the arched top of the foot

explanation.surface: Behaving as the soldiers of the other clue do when they march.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is the foot soldiers, who march 'in step'; 'on foot' also points to the instep, the upper arch of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching in time means being in step, and the instep is the arched middle part of the foot.

clue.text: Raised row round blockhead in river

indicators.note: round means the tier encloses the head letter of block

parts.note: a tier is one of a set of rows rising above another, as in a stadium
the head, or first letter, of block is B

explanation.surface: An elevated row of seats surrounds a fool in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhead' looks like a fool, but it is the head of 'block', its first letter. 'round' puts B inside TIER. The Tiber is the river through Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the Italian river on which Rome stands.

clue.text: Holiday diversion for clubman

parts.note: a seaside swim is a holiday pastime, and the word splits as a club, a bat, followed by a man, he

explanation.surface: Something to amuse a club member on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the word reads BAT (club) + HE (man), the 'clubman'. A bathe is the British word for a swim in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A swim in the sea is a classic seaside holiday pastime.

clue.text: I'd enter the result, that's obvious

indicators.note: enter means the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: the event is the outcome, as in 'in the event'
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they will record the outcome, which is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' signals the container. 'I'd enter' reads as someone's intention to record something, not as two letters going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain to see is apparent, clear or manifest.

clue.text: Music for song about eastern races

indicators.note: about means the song surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: an aria is a song for solo voice in opera
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the famous series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A tune for singing deals with races in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races, a common crossword abbreviation for races.
explanation.definitionFit: An arietta is a short, light aria, a piece of vocal music.

clue.text: Deity, returns money-order ?

indicators.note: returns says the money and the order are read backwards together

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A god sends back a postal money order.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM plus OM gives SUMOM, which 'returns' turns into MOMUS. 'money-order' suggests a postal order; it is two separate pieces. The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Momus was the Greek god of mockery and criticism.

clue.text: Church people fill in part of a manuscript

indicators.note: fill in means the church and the people go inside the word part

parts.note: taken as written
men means people, as in the men of a town

explanation.surface: Churchgoers complete a section of an old handwritten document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fill in' signals the container. 'part of' looks like a selection signal, but 'part' is a piece and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A document written on prepared animal skin is itself called a parchment, an old manuscript.
